newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila court stops campaign to extend Ramos term.
newsitem.headline: Manila court stops campaign to extend Ramos term.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Friday issued a temporary restraining order on organisers of a campaign to extend the term of President Fidel Ramos beyond 1998.

The court, responding to a petition filed by opposition leader Miriam Defensor Santiago, also restrained the Commission on Elections from hearing further petitions to "lift the term limits of elected officials (through) people's initiatives".

The Constitution limits the president to one six-year term and also restricts the time in office of other elected officials. Ramos, who took power in 1992, has said he does not want to stand for re-election in 1998.

But a citizens group led by former Ambassador Alberto Pedrosa and his wife has started a signature campaign to extend the term of Ramos, saying the economic reforms started by the president are in danger of withering away if he leaves office.
The couple have said they will raise the required five million signatures to force the Commission on Elections to hold a plebiscite on whether or not the Constitutional term limits should be amended.
The court asked the Pedrosa couple and the commission to reply to its order within 10 days.
Santiago, a senator and leader of the opposition People's Reform Party, lost to Ramos in the 1992 presidential elections.
